newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Airways cargo workers end strike.
newsitem.headline: Thai Airways cargo workers end strike.

text.p: Nearly 1,500 air cargo workers of Thai Airways International Plc went back to work on Wednesday, ending a two-day strike that paralysed cargo shipments from dozens of airlines, a union member said.

A member of the Thai Airways Employees Association said representatives of the union and the government reached an agreement late on Tuesday to halt a controversial government plan to launch a new Thai air cargo carrier. Government officials were not immediately available for comment.
"We resumed work after our representatives reached an agreement with the government...to halt the plan to set up a joint venture air cargo service," union spokesman Pirachat Tienson told Reuters.

He said the government agreed not to take disciplinary action against the strikers who stopped working and held protests in front of Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's office to protest the government's October 15 decision to launch a new carrier.
Workers feared the introduction of the new carrier, Thai Air Cargo Co Ltd, could affect their jobs.
Pirachat said the government agreed that all workers would continue in their current status as employees of Thai Airways International.
